surfaces.says: Codex reads AGENTS.md at the repository root as project instructions, and one agent definition per TOML file under .codex/agents/ -- name, description and developer_instructions as strings. Taken from the product's documentation; a claim until a run of the product is observed reading what was served. It reads hooks at .codex/hooks.json (events pre_tool_use / post_tool_use, matcher apply_patch); the event names are measured by inspection of codex-cli 0.153.2 and post_write_block is proven by receipt on a prior hand-built system, but every tool_input.* key and the patch grammar in `hands` are UNVERIFIED -- ordered so a wrong guess misses (and the judge then refuses as unjudged) rather than mis-binds. Codex has NOT proven pre_exec_block, so the judge is wired AFTER the write: a refusal there flags the change to the model, it does not prevent it (ADR-017 decision 5). Scoped law: it builds its instruction chain by reading AGENTS.md from the project root down to the working directory, one file per directory, later (deeper) files appearing after and overriding earlier ones -- taken from the product's AGENTS.md documentation; UNVERIFIED on this machine, and a scope only binds when the session's working directory lies at or below it (a file edited below it from a root session is not claimed to see it). Skills: one directory per skill under .agents/skills/ holding SKILL.md (front matter `name`, `description`, optional `allowed-tools`) and its supporting files -- taken from the product's skills documentation (fetched 2026-10-16); a claim until a run is observed loading a served skill. MCP: `[mcp_servers.<name>]` tables in a project .codex/config.toml, read for trusted projects (stdio `command`/`args`/`env_vars`, http `url`/`bearer_token_env_var`/`env_http_headers`, `enabled_tools` as an allow list) -- taken from the product's MCP documentation (fetched 2026-10-16); a claim until a run is observed. The kit serves one span of that file. Session lifecycle: by inspection of the installed codex-cli 0.154.0 binary (2026-10-16), its hook vocabulary names session_start, session_end, user_prompt_submit, subagent_start, subagent_stop, pre_compact, post_compact and permission_request beside pre_tool_use and post_tool_use (and the same events in PascalCase, Stop among them) -- a CLAIM of the event names only. What each event hands its hook on stdin, whether a session-start hook's stdout reaches the model, whether a stop hook's exit refuses the stop, and whether a sub-agent's model and usage are in any record a hook can read, are NOT measured -- so this surface declares no `context` and no `ledger`, serves no session-start, stop or sub-agent-stop hook, and the stop gate does not hold a Codex session. The first observed receipt of each event is what turns one of them into a declaration.

limits.says: Codex reads at most project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB by default) of AGENTS.md -- from the product's configuration documentation; a claim until measured
